chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil, from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Marry the dull/simple-minded women who do not exhibit enmity (towards the Ahl al-Bayt) and the weak/submissive ones.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْبُلْهِ: The simple-minded, dull, or less sharp-witted (often implying ease of management)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفَاتِ: The weak, submissive, or humble ones
key_terms.تَنْصِبُ: She exhibits enmity or pride (specifically towards the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What does 'al-bulh' mean in the context of selecting a wife in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Baqir (AS) advises selecting wives who are 'al-bulh' (often interpreted as simple, gentle, or less argumentative) and 'al-mustad'afat' (submissive or humble), specifically those who do not 'nasaba' (exhibit enmity or pride, particularly towards the Ahl al-Bayt). This guidance highlights the importance of temperamental compatibility and humility in maintaining marital harmony, reflecting the Shia emphasis on choosing partners who align with spiritual and social values.
